title: Incidental Holds, Liability Caps and Credit Validity, Resort Lodging
content:
The finance office publishes five figures against each Resort Lodging unit type covering what is held at check-in, how long the hold stands, how far liability for damage runs and how long lodging credit lasts.

The incidental hold is the amount in USD held against the lead guest's payment method at check-in for incidentals and damage. The release period is the number of business days after departure within which the incidental hold is released. The damage liability cap is the most the guest is held liable for in damage to the unit beyond the incidental hold. The smoking penalty is the charge in USD raised where the unit is found to have been smoked in. The credit validity period is the number of calendar days from issue within which lodging credit must be spent.

| Unit type | Incidental hold (USD) | Release period (business days) | Damage liability cap (USD) | Smoking penalty (USD) | Credit validity (calendar days) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Base Village Inn Room | 150.00 | 5 | 2500.00 | 350.00 | 365 |
| Slopeside Studio | 250.00 | 5 | 4000.00 | 450.00 | 365 |
| Slopeside One-Bedroom Residence | 350.00 | 5 | 6000.00 | 550.00 | 365 |
| Slopeside Two-Bedroom Residence | 500.00 | 7 | 8000.00 | 650.00 | 365 |
| Mountain Lodge Suite | 500.00 | 7 | 8000.00 | 650.00 | 365 |
| Summit Penthouse Residence | 1500.00 | 10 | 25000.00 | 1500.00 | 540 |
| Private Mountain Chalet | 5000.00 | 14 | 75000.00 | 3500.00 | 540 |

### Notes on the schedule

The incidental hold and the damage liability cap are different figures with different purposes: the hold is the sum taken at check-in, the cap the ceiling on liability beyond it, and for the Summit Penthouse Residence they stand at 1500.00 USD and 25000.00 USD. The release period is counted in business days, the credit validity period in calendar days, and the two are never read on the same calendar. Two unit types carry the longer credit validity of 540 days; the other five carry 365.
